goals: Euro-BioImaging ERIC is a pan-European research infrastructure offering open access to state-of-the-art technologies, training and data services for biological and biomedical imaging. Its mission is to empower researchers across borders and scientific domains and to facilitate innovative, world-class research. Euro-BioImaging provides i) physical access to more than 120 cutting-edge technologies across 330 research facilities, organised in 41 Nodes in 18 countries plus the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL), and ii) virtual access to image data services, including repositories for sharing and re-using reference image datasets. It shares expertise on imaging methods and technologies, promotes training and FAIR data management for users and service providers, and supports researchers at all career stages, for example through travel grants for conferences and courses. Euro-BioImaging was awarded ESFRI Landmark status in 2018 and was established as an ERIC at the end of 2019.

goals:
The BOOST research consortium (2021-2027) aims to mainstream biodiversity protection and enable a just transition towards ecological compensation. Ecological compensation refers to the compensation of environmental damage caused by ecologically harmful activities through concrete improvements and actions in nature . 

The three impact objectives of the Ecological Compensation in a Just Transition to a Net Neutrality of Nature (BOOST) project are:

- Improving national and international understanding of ecological compensation;
- Development of an ecological compensation system; and
-Mainstreaming ecological compensation.

Together, the goals aim to design, build and implement an ecological compensation system based on researched information in Finland.

The FBA is a public entity that is founded by law (The Finnish Advocates Act 496/1958), and the statutes of the FBA have been verified by the Finnish Ministry of Justice (Statutes of the Finnish Bar Association 540/2012). The FBA has statutory responsibilities and acts as “indirect public administration” handling its responsibilities in the Finnish Legal system. These responsibilities include for example approving new Attorneys-at-law and supervising the professional activities of Attorneys-at-law, Licensed Trial Counsels and Public Legal Aid attorneys. The Finnish legal system does not include a monopoly on Attorneys-at-law.

The FBA is not a trade union and does not represent interests of any commercial nature nor its members. All activities and actions taken by the FBA aim to ensure the realization of the principle of Rule of Law and impartiality of the lawyers representing and defending clients before the courts of law as well as access to justice and fundamental and human rights.

Luonnonvarakeskus (Natural Resources Institute Finland, Luke) is an independent research institute operating under the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry of Finland (MMM). Luke conducts scientific research, provides expert services and statistics, and participates extensively in competitive national and international research and innovation programs.

Luke resolves challenges in the sustainable and profitable use of renewable natural resources in 3 research programs. Every year, Luke has about 600 research projects in progress, roughly 100 of which are EU projects. In 2025, Luke’s researchers published 764 peer-reviewed scientific publications. Research accounts for approx. 70% of Luke’s activities.

In addition, Luke has statutory duties, and it compiles Finland’s official food and natural resources statistics.

Luke’s activities are guided by Luke’s strategy and the performance agreement signed annually with MMM. Luke’s official duties are defined in EU and national regulations.

Clarifi Oy’s areas of interest include the development and implementation of EU regulatory frameworks affecting medical technologies, digital health, biotechnology and food innovation.

Relevant legislation and policy initiatives include:

- European Health Data Space Regulation (EHDS), particularly implementation, interoperability, secondary use of health data and implications for SMEs.
- Medical Device Regulation (EU) 2017/745 and In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Device Regulation (EU) 2017/746.
- Artificial Intelligence Act (EU) 2024/1689, particularly its interaction with medical device regulation and digital health innovation.
- General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679, particularly the responsible processing of health-related data.
- EU Novel Food Regulation (EU) 2015/2283 and associated regulatory frameworks for innovative food ingredients.
- EU research and innovation policies, including Horizon Europe and initiatives supporting the commercialisation of research.

Clarifi is particularly interested in evidence-based policymaking, regulatory coherence, proportionate implementation and meaningful participation by SMEs and emerging technology developers.

goals: The Integrated Carbon Observation System (ICOS) is a distributed European-wide Research Infrastructure producing high-precision data on greenhouse gas concentrations in the atmosphere, as well as on carbon fluxes between the atmosphere, the land surface, and the ocean. ICOS provides standardized and open data from more than 180 measurement stations across 16 European countries. ICOS provides data that researchers transform into scientific knowledge to improve our understanding of the Earth system. Evidence-based knowledge on carbon emissions and sinks contributes to the UN Sustainable Development Goals and EU Societal Challenges, especially climate change. ICOS is a major European research infrastructure contributing to the global network of international climate organizations. The knowledge generated by the use of ICOS data supports the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the Paris Agreement and the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCC).

goals:
The organization's mission is to develop and commercialize novel, sustainable food and feed ingredients produced via microbial fermentation using renewable inputs.
Our activities relate primarily to EU food law and biotechnology regulation, in particular the authorisation, safety assessment, and regulatory framework for novel foods and novel food ingredients under Regulation (EU) 2015/2283.
We also follow EU-level developments concerning food safety risk assessment, sustainable food systems, and industrial biotechnology, insofar as these impact the regulatory requirements, market access, and labelling of fermentation-derived food ingredients within the European Union.
Engagement with EU institutions is relevant to ensure that evolving EU legislation and implementing practices are informed by up-to-date scientific evidence and reflect the specific characteristics of fermentation-based food production.

Tämä on konkreettinen esimerkki siitä, miten digitalisaatio parantaa hoidon saatavuutta ja vaikuttavuutta.

goals:
Agion.ai builds the control layer for AI-native organisations. Our goal is to make agentic AI safe, governable and useful in real operational environments — especially for enterprises and public-sector organisations that need security, auditability, compliance and digital sovereignty.

We provide an Agent Governance Platform that enables organisations to deploy, manage and audit AI agents at scale. The platform turns business goals, policies and compliance requirements into executable operating rules through Mission-as-Code, Governance-as-Code, Dynamic Trust and Radical Transparency. This means agent actions can be validated before they happen, autonomy can be adjusted based on trust, and every decision can be traced and audited.

Our remit is not simply to automate tasks, but to help organisations move safely from fragmented, human-only workflows toward AI-native operating models where people set direction, define boundaries and maintain accountability, while governed agents execute.

legislativeProposals: Agion.ai primarily targets the EU AI Act, especially requirements for high-risk AI systems, transparency, human oversight, technical documentation, audit trails and accountable deployment of AI agents. In practice, Agion turns these obligations into machine-enforceable governance controls, including mission scoping, risk classification, human-in-the-loop approval, data-access restrictions, retention rules and auditable execution logs.

Porin laitoksen on arvioitu tuottavan noin 9 000 tonnia vanadiinia vuodessa, mikä vastaa noin 5–6 prosenttia koko globaalista tuotannosta ja 60 prosenttia Euroopan tarvitsemasta vanadiinista.

IQM is the European leader in superconducting quantum computers. We build quantum computers for research laboratories and supercomputing centers. 

In 2018 a group of ambitious scientists took the (quantum) leap to turn their theory to practice. The team started with breakthroughs in developing the tech towards large-scale quantum processors. Teemme lähetys-, kehitysyhteis-, rauhan- ja humanitääristä työtä 24 maassa ympäri maailmaa. Teemme työtä, jotta tavoitamme heikoimmassa asemassa olevat, sorretut ja syrjityt. Työtämme ohjaavat YK:n kestävän kehityksen tavoitteet sekä kansainväliset ihmisoikeusperiaatteet. 

Teemme työtä yhteensä noin 970 ammattilaisen voimin eri puolilla maailmaa. Kehitysyhteistyöstämme hyötyy vuosittain yli 2 miljoonaa ihmistä.

NEOT Oy is a fuel procurement company operating in the Baltic Sea region, whose ambitions are supplying fuel sector with increasing amount the sustainable renewable energy in transport sector. The overall target is to diminish the need for fossil fuels and thus reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions while helping mitigate Climate Change.

NEOT (North European Oil Trade) is a significant independent fuel procurement company in the Baltic Sea region. We specialise in oil and renewable products wholesale in Finland, Sweden and Norway and actively operate on the global trading market. We aim to supply the transport sector with increasing amount the sustainable renewable energy solutions. The overall target is to reduce green house gas emissions resulting from transportation to help achieving EU climate targets.

goals:
Wolt is Helsinki-based technology company that provides an online platform to connect people looking to order restaurant food, groceries, and a wide variety of retail categories with people in their communities interested in selling and delivering them. We call this local commerce.

Our service brings convenience to customers, but also creates economic opportunities for local restaurants and retailers selling their goods over our platform and for independent couriers providing services to Wolt.

We currently operate in 32 countries (20 of which are EU Member States) and over 1000 cities, serving goods from over 150,000 merchants with over 300,000 courier partners to more than 55 million registered users, and employ more than 13,000 people in our offices across our markets.

goals: Puro.earth is the world's leading carbon-crediting platform for durable carbon dioxide removal (CDR). Via the Puro Standard’s rigorous carbon credit methodologies, suppliers that remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to durable storages for at least 100 years are certified and issued CO2 Removal Certificates (CORCs) into the transparent Puro Registry. CORCs are then purchased by ambitious corporations like Microsoft, Shopify, and Zurich Insurance, to help address climate change and neutralize residual carbon emissions. In 2021, Nasdaq acquired a majority stake in Puro.earth and together they are driving forward the carbon removal industry, enabling new revenue streams to accelerate carbon removal.
